solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Opposing court agreement

parts.note: contra is Latin-derived for against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A legal dispute in which a court's agreement is being challenged by the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding deal between parties is a synonym for an agreement.

clue.text: Tailor to repeat work

indicators.note: to tailor something is to alter it, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A tailor told to redo the same job again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' is a verb signalling the anagram of TO REPEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera, and opus means work, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: Piece on best books penned by factual writer

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as animals in a pen, so these pieces go inside the word for factual

parts.note: true means factual
a man is a piece in chess or draughts
to cap is to outdo or best
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An article about bestselling books written by a non-fiction author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factual writer' is a sly nod to the author of In Cold Blood, which he called a non-fiction novel; 'penned by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American author of In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: Another one playing Hamlet, perhaps

indicators.note: playing about with letters signals a rearrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Yet another actor taking on the role of Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the anagram of ANOTHER plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a flawed, hesitant protagonist, an example of a hero lacking heroic qualities.

clue.text: Stream rubbish after withdrawing regular payment

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the word for rubbish is read backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
rent is the regular payment for a home

explanation.surface: Garbage pours out in a flood once the regular payment is stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after withdrawing' makes TOR; the surface wants 'withdrawing regular payment' to be a cancelled direct debit.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, violent flow of water, a kind of stream.

clue.text: Desperado with wounded flanks

indicators.note: flanks means lies on either side of, so the word for wounded goes around the next piece

parts.note: bit means wounded by teeth, as a dog bit someone
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: An outlaw shot in the sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' reads as an adjective but stands for the past tense bit, as in bitten by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a violent outlaw, a near synonym for a desperado.

clue.text: Story of Biblical character under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming below, so the pressure letter goes first

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
Lot is the nephew of Abraham in Genesis

explanation.surface: A tale of a figure from the Bible who is under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a novel is its storyline, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Introduced quiet escape around river delta

indicators.note: around means the quiet escape surrounds the river letter

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
to elude is to escape
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone slipped quietly away across a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside PELUDE after its P, and D is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To prelude something is to introduce it or serve as its preface.

clue.text: Wise old count initially ignored queen

indicators.note: the first letter of the count's name is dropped, the initial being ignored

parts.note: Count Dracula is the vampire count of Bram Stoker's novel
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An elderly nobleman was shrewd enough to snub the queen at first meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' is not a verb here: it is the vampire Count DRACULA, who loses his D to leave RACULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular pronouncements are prophetic and full of wisdom, like those of an oracle.

clue.text: A united country

parts.note: per means a, as in so much per head or a head

explanation.surface: A nation described as one united whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' gives PER, as in 'twice a day' = 'twice per day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation, a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Post occupied by tense, furious European restaurant worker

indicators.note: the post is filled by the following pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: post is letters delivered, the mail
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
red-hot describes someone burning with anger

explanation.surface: A furious European waiter's post is taken over by tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job title but means the mail; 'occupied by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A maître d'hôtel is the head waiter who runs the dining room, a restaurant employee.

clue.text: Stop, cross because senior officer admitted to failing short course

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so these pieces go into the jumbled letters
failing means breaking down, so the letters are jumbled
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: X is the cross sign
for means because, as in 'for he was tired'
DCI is a Detective Chief Inspector, a senior police officer

explanation.surface: An angry senior officer, failing a short course, is told to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts COURSE to COURS and 'failing' jumbles it to ORCUS; XFORDCI goes in after the O. Oxford Circus is a London Underground station, a stop on the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford Circus is a station on the London Underground, so it is a stop on the Tube.

clue.text: Immediately somewhat flat on cello

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cellist hears a note played somewhat flat and wants it fixed straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means straight away, without any delay.

clue.text: Informed current editor after seizure, working in retirement

indicators.note: the current and editor pieces come after the reversed run
retiring means drawing back, so the two words before are read backwards together

parts.note: a fit is a seizure, as in an epileptic fit
on means working, as a machine that is on
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor was told the news after having a fit while working in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' gives NOTIF; the surface pictures a retired editor, but retirement here means turning backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be notified is to be told officially, so the participle means informed.

clue.text: Accompany someone dismissing northern language

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter for northern is removed

parts.note: to tag along is to go along with someone

explanation.surface: A companion who brushes off a northerner and goes along with someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the main tongue of the Philippines, an example of a language.

clue.text: Inconsiderate head of theatre with advice to overworked thesp?

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a busy actor might be told to act less

explanation.surface: A theatre manager tells an exhausted actor to cut back on work.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'thesp' is a thespian, an actor, who might be told to ACT LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactless means lacking tact, so inconsiderate of others' feelings.

clue.text: Obtained unpleasant church doctrine at first

parts.note: sour means disagreeable or unpleasant
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone acquired a nasty church teaching early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourced is used of goods or information acquired from a supplier, so it means obtained.

clue.text: Capsize concealed vessel bypassing cape

indicators.note: bypassing means skipping round, so the cape letter is left out

parts.note: covert means hidden or concealed
C is the map abbreviation for cape
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: A hidden ship tipped over while steering round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but it is an URN; COVERT loses its C to give OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a boat is to make it capsize, turning it upside down.

clue.text: Diverse vote for keeping Conservative in charge

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the Conservative letter goes into the word for vote for

parts.note: to elect is to vote for

explanation.surface: A varied ballot in which a Tory stays in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals the insertion; the surface's ballot picture hides that 'in charge' is just an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic means drawing on a wide range of sources, so varied or diverse.

clue.text: Do complain about drunken outburst

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for complain goes round the outburst

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is the sound of a drunk's hiccup

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a drunk's outburst at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a hairdo, not a party: a mohican is a hairstyle of a central strip of spiky hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mohican is a haircut, and a do is a hairdo, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Look set on company leaving island state

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece set on another comes after it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: the island letter leaves the word for set, so it is removed

parts.note: a radio is a receiving set

explanation.surface: A firm is looking to move its business off an island to a mainland state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' gives RADO: 'set' is a radio set, not a verb, and 'island' is just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty United States, an example of a state.

clue.text: Extremely atypical tree growing high on a mountain

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters of the following word

parts.note: a pine is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A very unusual tree found high on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine plants are those that grow at high altitude above the tree line.

clue.text: Is outstanding social media platform about to be controlled by untrustworthy people?

indicators.note: being controlled by means being held inside, so these letters go within the untrustworthy people

parts.note: eels are slippery, so shifty people are called eels
X is the platform formerly called Twitter
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Asks whether a big social network is about to fall into the hands of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: X and C sit inside EELS after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to stand out or be superior, so the verb means is outstanding.

clue.text: Learner trips, breaking computer equipment

indicators.note: breaking signals that the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A novice stumbles and smashes some of the office's computer kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the anagram signal: LEARNER and TRIPS are rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer is a device attached to computers, a piece of computer equipment.

clue.text: Endlessly short of money for personal cover

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: skint is British slang for penniless

explanation.surface: Constantly lacking money to pay for one's own insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for broke; without its end it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin is the body's outer covering, so a person's own cover.

clue.text: Time to probe peer who ran animal shelter

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so the letter for time is inserted

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the Olympic middle-distance runner, became Lord Coe, a peer

explanation.surface: An investigation into an aristocrat who once managed an animal sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Coe is the British Olympic runner turned peer; the surface wants 'ran' to mean managed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cote is a small shed for birds or sheep, as in dovecote, a shelter for animals.

clue.text: Republic of Ireland turned left, filling bored socialist's heart

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so these pieces are put within the word for bored

parts.note: to sink a well is to bore it, so sank means bored

indicators.note: turned says the letters for Ireland are read backwards
the heart is the middle letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Irish politics: the Republic swung left, filling the core of a weary socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives RI, and 'heart' gives A; 'Republic of Ireland' looks like one phrase but is split, with 'Republic' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is officially the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, an example of a republic.

clue.text: Nun chose cultivated plant

indicators.note: cultivated, as soil is worked over, signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun picked out a plant to grow in the convent garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' is the anagram signal for NUN and CHOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonesuch is the black medick, a clover-like plant of the pea family.
